topic: Anti-patterns + community failure modes for multi-agent Claude Code

claims.claim: Anthropic's own multi-agent research system initially spawned 50 subagents for simple queries; fix was explicit effort tiers and delegation rules in the prompt, not better models.
Every subagent pays ~20-50k token entry tax (system + CLAUDE.md + MCP tool descriptions) before useful work; 5 parallel subagents = 100-250k pure overhead.
Anti-pattern 'Don't delegate understanding': subagent summaries destroy nuance; keep reasoning in main context, delegate only flood-producing side-quests.
Claude Opus 4.6 has a documented tendency to over-spawn subagents by default; fix is explicit 'do not spawn unless asked' in CLAUDE.md plus plan-mode gates.
Resumed subagents lose user prompts (Issue #11712); they hallucinate 'corrections' trying to infer original task. Workaround: write task spec to file, re-load on resume.
Subagents with tools allowlist that mismatches their skill instructions will hallucinate tool outputs silently rather than erroring.
Agent sprawl: multiple dev sessions each spawning own teams with no coordinator is emerging organizational anti-pattern; requires explicit merge ownership.
Token waste is more often model-misallocation than prompt-inefficiency: extractors/search/grep should be Haiku; only reasoning/synthesis warrant Opus.
Claude Code multi-agent UX is macOS-first: Windows users stuck with in-process mode + worktree symlink issues (cross-ref R3+R6).
Multi-agent systems consume ~15x tokens vs chat, ~4x vs single-agent-tool-use; only justified when outcome value is at least that much greater.
Auto-selection of custom subagents via description field is unreliable; only explicit invocation (by name in user message or slash command) routes reliably.
Wide-and-flat hierarchy (6 subagents under one orchestrator) is worse than narrow-and-deep (2 leads, each 2-3 specialists); orchestrator cognition degrades at high fan-out.
Tool proliferation (>20 first-party tools) itself degrades agent performance; Anthropic's solution is progressive disclosure (skills referencing searchable files, specialist subagents).
Early multi-agent systems exhibit source-selection bias toward SEO content farms over authoritative academic/blog sources; requires explicit source-quality prompting.
Context-bleed-vs-miss is the core isolation tradeoff: tight scope misses cross-module context; loose scope contaminates peer work. Remedy: contract-driven boundaries + file locking.
Practical delegation depth limit is 2-3 levels even without recursion hard-limit at 1; token overhead compounds geometrically (27 leaves at fan-out 3 = 540k-1.35M token overhead).
Anthropic's #1 published principle for multi-agent prompt engineering: 'Think like your agents' - develop mental models through simulation before prompting.
GitHub Issue #4911 documents 15-76x token inflation for subagent-equivalent work (2-3k main session vs 153.8k subagent, 3m 32s).
'I remember this skill' trap: Claude describes a skill from training data rather than loading the skill file; produces confident stale instructions.
Broadcast abuse in Agent Teams: using broadcast for everything creates 5x context noise at 5 teammates; docs explicitly warn 'use sparingly'.
Memory substitution in routines: routines referencing other routines by name get described from training memory rather than invoked as fresh file reads.
Persona confusion: a routine given a persona in one turn leaks that persona into the next turn, contaminating subsequent reasoning.

conflicts_flagged.description: Opus over-spawn vs Sonnet under-spawn: Opus 4.6 spawns too eagerly, Sonnet sometimes fails to spawn even when appropriate. Different fixes per model.
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Model-specific guidance in synthesis: Opus needs 'do not spawn' restraint; Sonnet needs explicit 'use X subagent' invocation.

conflicts_flagged.description: Some community guides encourage subagents for all research tasks; Anthropic's 'Don't delegate understanding' cautions against it for reasoning-heavy work.
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Clarify split: delegate enumeration/search; keep reasoning inline.

gaps_flagged.description: No systematic benchmark comparing wide-flat vs narrow-deep orchestration hierarchies; community guidance is qualitative.
No official guidance on merging divergent work from parallel worktree-based agents - merge-time surprises anecdotal.
Broadcast vs message cost-per-teammate numbers not published.
